findings.finding: The empty-body check uses the same per-line runs_interpreter flag as the unterminated check, so every heredoc opened on a line that also runs `python -` is blamed on the interpreter (e.g. `python - < script.py && cat > out.txt <<'E'` + `E`). Rare; failing this way only blocks a command.
findings.suggestion: Accept as a documented known miss, or attribute each heredoc to its own segment. At minimum pin the behaviour with a test.

findings.finding: pending is a heterogeneous untyped 4-slot list mutated by magic index (pending[0][3] = True).
findings.suggestion: Keep tuples and track head body state in a local, or use a small dataclass.

findings.finding: Edited registry row has two incident parentheticals in one sentence; the colon attaches to the wrong clause; the row still says a closed `uv run python - <<'EOF' ... EOF` passes without stating non-empty; dated provenance is not docs content.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite: 'Denies a Bash command whose `python -` has no heredoc, pipe or `<` behind it, or whose heredoc feeding that line is never closed or is closed with an empty/whitespace-only body: the interpreter then waits on stdin forever.' Keep one short incident reference; say 'closed, non-empty'.
